subject: Service saturation: request for eligibility confirmation, raw evidence pull, and postmortem scheduling
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clearline-payments.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strange 503/429 surge during peak batch - potential SLO claim

Diego / Marissa,

We saw a sharp spike of 503 and 429 errors affecting our checkout traffic on 2027-08-29 between 22:45 and 23:09 UTC (US-WEST). Our telemetry shows ~8% of checkout attempts failed during that ~24 minute window which materially impacted our conversion funnel.

Can you confirm whether this event is covered under Redwood's availability SLOs and what evidence we should provide to support a credit? Our legal/procurement team is asking for the exact window you use for eligibility calculations and any raw traces/logs we should attach.

I can provide a short list of order IDs and a sample curl trace if helpful — attaching a csv of impacted order ids (impacted_orders_clearline_aug29.csv).

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Reliability
Clearline Payments

--

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clearline-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange 503/429 surge during peak batch - potential SLO claim

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. We're pulling telemetry now. A few immediate asks so we can validate eligibility quickly: 

1) Confirm the sample order IDs are from the 22:45–23:09 UTC window (you already attached file, thanks).
2) If you have any client-side traces (curl/wget headers) from failed attempts, please send them — they help align retries and error codes with our ingress logs.
3) We'll prepare a raw trace bundle from our side (kernel and request traces, autoscaler logs, kv-cache metrics). Can you confirm where to upload? We will put a redacted bundle in the Drive link below and share a signed evidence hash.

Prelim note: initial telemetry suggests a sustained enqueue backlog on the serving tier tied to autoscaler spinups in US-WEST. That can look like a "saturation" window rather than a single control-plane outage. Eligibility still may apply depending on the SLO definition for partial availability in your contract. I'll loop in Vivek & Laura to coordinate credits and PM scheduling.

Proposed timeline: we aim to deliver the raw Redwood trace bundle within 6 business hours and schedule a short postmortem call tomorrow. Does 10:00 AM PT Tue 2027-08-31 work for you?

Diego Fernandez
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange 503/429 surge during peak batch - potential SLO claim

Sanjay — we completed an initial evidence pull and uploaded a redacted bundle to the Drive link below. Bundle includes ingress request traces, autoscaler events, kv-cache eviction logs, and per-tenant token counts. Attachments: clearline-raw-trace-2027-08-30.tar.gz

Early findings (very preliminary):
- Autoscaler moved 3x in a 2-minute period at ~22:50–22:52 UTC causing transient queue growth and downstream 429s.
- KV-cache eviction pressure increased at 22:48 UTC which amplified tail latency for payloads that hit cold keys.
- There is no evidence of control-plane downtime; instead we see resource saturation and repeated scale events.

Questions for eligibility: is your SLO worded on per-request availability (501/503/429 as failures) or on a broadened latency SLO? If the former, this likely qualifies as an availability window; we'll need to align on the exact sample window you plan to claim to compute prorated credits.

Drive (restricted): https://drive.redwood.internal/teams/ops/CLR-9832/logs
Evidence hash (SHA256): 3f7c9b...fa12

I'll also attach a calendar invite for the postmortem.

Diego Fernandez

Sanjay / team — thank you for the fast signal and the patience while we pulled logs. I reviewed Diego's preliminary notes.

Next steps from Redwood: 
- We will produce a formal SLO eligibility memo by EOD tomorrow (2027-08-31) that documents the exact window used, the prorated credit calculation, and the telemetry slices.
- We will host a joint postmortem on Tue 2027-08-31 at 10:00 AM PT (invite attached: maple-postmortem-invite.ics). Please confirm a Clearline attendee (platform + procurement).
- If the SLO eligibility memo supports a credit, Marissa will draft the credit notice and coordinate DocuSign via the link below.

To be clear on expectations: given the telemetry shows autoscaler-induced saturation (not a control-plane down event), we may compute a proportional remedy under Section 4.2 of the contract. We will not pre-commit to a remedy until the full evidence review completes.

Action for Clearline: please reply with the name/email of your procurement contact and whether you want Redwood to proceed with redacted logs upload to your S3 (we can also send a signed SHA256 digest).

I'll be on the call and will accept follow-up questions.

— Vivek Kulkarni
